summary: This Best Current Practice document removes a limit on the number of Area Directors who manage an IETF Area. It updates RFC 2026 and RFC 2418.

plainLanguage.summary: This Best Current Practice removes the upper limit on Area Directors for an IETF Area. It changes two definitions so an Area can have one or more directors.

questions: how many area directors can an ietf area have
why was the area director limit removed
subtitle: Allows an IETF Area to have more than two Area Directors when needed.

tldr.problem: IETF rules limited each Area to one or two Area Directors, which conflicted with a proposal for an Area managed by three.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC changes the definitions in RFC 2026 and RFC 2418 from one or two Area Directors to one or more.
tldr.outcome: The change gives the IESG more flexibility in organizing work without changing what an Area does or asserting that more directors are always better.

today: RFC 7475 is a Best Current Practice, and the unit metadata lists no RFC that updates or obsoletes it. It updates RFC 2026 and RFC 2418.

sections.title: Scope and Intent
sections.content:
RFC 7475 updates RFC 2026 and RFC 2418 to remove the limit on the number of Area Directors who manage an IETF Area. The goal is to give the Internet Engineering Steering Group (IESG) more flexibility in organizing work.

The change does not alter the role of an Area and does not claim that having more than two Area Directors is a long-term optimum. The RFC says that if several Areas need more directors, the IESG should consider other ways to organize its work.
sections.plainLanguage: The change gives the IESG more choice in assigning Area Directors. It does not change what an Area is responsible for.

sections.title: Why the Limit Changed
sections.content:
The IESG had considered splitting and combining Areas, and one proposal would create an Area managed by three Area Directors. That conflicted with existing wording that allowed only one or two.

The RFC notes that the number of Area Directors has varied over time, including an earlier case with three in one Area. It says the Nominating Committee's review of approximately half of IESG positions each year is unchanged.
sections.plainLanguage: A proposal for three directors did not fit the old rule. The RFC removes that conflict and leaves the existing position-review schedule unchanged.

sections.title: The Updated Definition
sections.content:
In Section 14 of RFC 2026, the phrase saying that an Area is managed by "one or two Area Directors" is replaced with "one or more Area Directors".

In Section 1 of RFC 2418, the same change is made to the sentence about how each IETF Area is managed. The RFC also says that informational documents describing the old limit should be considered updated by this specification. It has no direct Internet security implications.
sections.plainLanguage: Both documents now say that an Area has one or more Area Directors. They no longer set a maximum number.
